definition: The (dead-end) sentence-alignment library this project tried first; see voice/README.md.
To match spoken audio to its source text, timestamp by timestamp.
The physical shaping of speech sounds by the tongue, lips, and jaw.
The rhythmic flow of speech.
A speech sound made by full or partial closure of the vocal tract, e.g. /p/, /t/, /k/.
The choice and clarity of words in speech.
A sound formed by the combination of two vowels in a single syllable, e.g. the 'oy' in 'boy'.
To play recorded audio back after capturing it — the vecho.sh loop this app's Voice tab ports.
To pronounce words clearly and distinctly.
The ability to speak smoothly and readily.
Grapheme-to-phoneme: converting written text into its expected pronunciation.
Google's open-weight small language model family; this app's on-device LLM tab targets a Gemma 3 1B int4 build.
The rise and fall of pitch while speaking.
The programming language this Android app is written in.
Google AI Edge's on-device LLM runtime and model file format used by this app's LLM tab.
An ffmpeg audio filter that normalizes perceived loudness; part of vecho.sh's desktop cleanup chain, not yet ported here.
A word that phonetically imitates the sound it describes, e.g. 'buzz'.
The smallest unit of sound that distinguishes one word from another.
The way in which a word is spoken.
The ONNX-based speech toolkit this project's desktop STT/TTS (stt.py, mdtalk.sh) is built on.
The relative emphasis given to certain syllables in a word.
A unit of pronunciation with one vowel sound, forming a word or part of a word.
A written representation of spoken language.
A speech sound made with an open vocal tract, e.g. /a/, /i/, /u/.
